html:
The Battle of Grunwald, called Tannenberg by Germans, was fought on 15 July 1410 in Prussia, where the armies of Poland and Lithuania under King Władysław II Jagiełło and Grand Duke Vytautas defeated the Teutonic Knights.

It was one of the largest battles of medieval Europe. The Grand Master Ulrich von Jungingen and most of the order's leaders were killed. The Poles failed to take the order's capital at Malbork, and the peace of 1411 changed little land, but the order never recovered its power. The union of Poland and Lithuania, begun at Krewo, became the leading power of the region. The victory is a symbol of Polish and Lithuanian pride, painted on a huge canvas by Jan Matejko in 1878.
